deviations_from_the_spec: Self-contained tests: the three files do NOT import tcb/test/helpers.mjs (it did not exist when I wrote them and its behaviour is only sketched in CONTRACT 4.11). Each file carries its own makeRoot/runScript/transcript writer/sleeper/ledger writer (own canonicalize + sha256 for the hash chain, own verifier). They do import tcb/scripts/lib.mjs in two places only, for lib.checkFormat(root, 'status'|'tasks', value) (status T1, handover T1).

Each test copies tcb/{scripts,schemas,profiles,settings,agents,briefs} and cost-inputs.json/denylist.txt from tcb-build/tcb into its temp root and runs <root>/tcb/scripts/<name>.mjs. thresholds.json is written per root from fixtures/<script>/_testdata.json (all CONTRACT 3.20 names, test values: delta_ms 50, coalesce_ticks 0, stall_calls/hang_ticks 1000, alarm_ms 100, user_files [], transcripts_root = <root>/transcripts); a test lowers only the threshold it exercises.
Fixtures are files named with a leading underscore directly in tcb/fixtures/<script>/ (not case folders with case.json), so selftest's one-folder-per-case scan should not mistake them for cases.
Spend-sensitive tests use input-only usage (400 tokens per call = 1200 for 3 calls) so unweighted total and weighted cost agree.

Event assertions are tolerant about the class field: a line matches when data.class or data.code equals the slug or the number. Only 'stall' + urgent:true is asserted as spec'd (T2). Event key format is only checked as containing the task and (T14) a later onset tick in the last '|' segment.
stdout 'ok' is asserted only for exit 0 (true); for wake exits (10-30) the contract does not say.

Extra tests beyond the numbered behaviours, named X1..X8: watch X1 class 25 (zombie spend past Z with no READY), X2 repair READY -> 12 and voids stall, X3 W_star_child gate -> 15, X4 checker batch 14 (needs cards in store/objects + witnessed status lines), X5 usage 66, X6 intake stale ce 64, X7 design-check has no stall counter, X8 coordinator W_quality -> 15 before 16; handover X1 usage (init --ce, bad session, missing flags -> 66). Also T19 variants (3 ends intake with 3; snap --new only when f5_given) and T13 intent --text-file sha / path-outside-root, T14 boundary 500/501/empty quote.
watch T3 'start evaluation does not count a hang tick' is asserted via a default-mode run with --interval-ms 50: exit 21 must come with ticks_total 2 and hang_ticks 2.
watch T10 forges run/watcher.json (ticks_total 100, dead pid) so fails 5 and 40 ticks apart can be placed against W_cc_ticks 30.
lib_change_requests: None required. Note for the library/helpers builder: if tcb/test/helpers.mjs ships, these three files do not use it, so its makeRoot is not exercised by them.

selftest.mjs: its fixture scan should skip files and folders whose name starts with '_' (my fixtures are _testdata.json, _split-call-*.jsonl, _three-calls.jsonl directly inside fixtures/watch, fixtures/status, fixtures/handover).
not_testable_without_the_app: watch: a background command's exit reaching the coordinator's turn, also during sleep or after a ce change (item 5) - skipped test NA1, reason 'needs the app'.
watch: Node timers and the PC across suspend, one sleep of Delta = one tick (item 6) - skipped NA2.
watch: real transcripts matching the parser, a real session's window in its transcript (item 7) - skipped NA3, NA4.

status: a real session's transcript appearing in projectDirName(folder) with that cwd soon after start (item 7) - skipped NA1; the watcher's and alarm's exits reaching the coordinator (item 5) - skipped NA2.

handover: the old coordinator woken by a late exit being refused by every writing script (item 5), the owner starting the successor from the brief, the old watcher/alarm reaching their next ce check and exiting 64 - skipped NA1-NA3; NA4 (a row reaching admitted/started/bound between the pre-check and the lock) is skipped because it is a two-party race that cannot be ordered from a test.
open_points: The tests were written before the three scripts, lib.mjs, helpers.mjs and most schemas existed in tcb-build/tcb, so they have never run green. I only ran them against the missing scripts: all 54 watch / 29 status / 22 handover tests (4/2/4 skipped) fail with 'Cannot find module' or an exit-code mismatch, none with a TypeError or ReferenceError in the test code, temp roots were cleaned up, the intake stub was run by hand and works, and the 50 MB generator takes about 80 ms. First real run will show mismatches between my reading of the spec and the code; judge each against the spec before changing either side.

Behaviours turned into tests only approximately: (a) watch T22 'reads only the new bytes' is checked through counters, not a read spy or timing: the first 2 MB of the 50 MB file is overwritten in place before tick 2 and calls must still be 203 and end_byte the new size. (b) status T9 (epoch moved between the table read and the update) is ordered with a fixed 4 s sleep while a live run.lock holder blocks the script; the final state asserted (fenced row skipped, other row started, one started line, exit 0) also holds if the script read the table after the edit, so the race itself may not always be exercised. (c) handover raise's re-check inside the lock (a row reaching admitted/started/bound after step 1 -> exit 6, nothing written) has no test: skipped NA4. (d) status T16: dry-run result is compared with the real run by exit code and result key set only, not deep equality.

Behaviours in the specs not tested: watch exit 70 'restart the watcher' on an uncaught error (no way to inject one); status --endturn exit 2 proc-unavailable and exit 2 schema-version; status build with proc list failure (anomaly proc-unavailable); status anomalies lock-orphan, ledger-torn, zombie-write, ready-unparseable, watcher-stale-ce, alarm-dead (only watcher-dead and several-sessions are tested); status `next` = owner for 'zombie spend over Z' (only failed and limit are tested); status reconcile's step of setting session on non-current attempts; handover init's ledger lines when a lock-break/torn-tail precedes coord-init; handover raise `proc-unavailable` exit 2 and `no-coordinator` exit 2 for raise/bind without coord.json (only bind/raise with corrupt coord = 67 is tested).

Format assumptions the tests make that the contract leaves open: attempts[].folder is the relative posix path 'wt/<task>-e<e>' (replace spec T3); nullable row/attempt fields are written as null rather than omitted; schema_version 1 is written in coord/tasks/acked/alarm/watcher/stop-sample/intent files but not in lock records or READY.json; --root is passed as the native backslash path while transcripts_root is written with forward slashes; a transcript cwd is path.join(root,'wt','<task>-e1') (backslashes) and its project folder is that path with : \ / . _ space replaced by '-'; the card in store/objects is canonical bytes named c_<first 16 hex of sha256>; for variant()/intakeCandidates the tests supply both the stored card object and a card_status.jsonl 'witnessed' line (X4, T2 second test), which is the part most likely to need adjusting if lib reads them differently.

watch T2/T3/T4 take the first tick on a transcript with zero calls so that the unspecified first-observation semantics of V_min (set on tick 1, new calls not counted) cannot matter; the tests assume stall counting starts at the second tick.

watch T18 relies on stub scripts the test writes over harvest/commit/snap/witness/promote/tms/status in the root's own tcb/scripts; the stub holds harvest until tmp/release exists (30 s cap) so a second tick can be made while the intake is alive; the test waits for the intake pid to end (tasklist) before deleting the root. Liveness of the intake pid is checked with tasklist, never by signalling.
watch T20 uses real sleeps inside the script (first alarm 5-6 s, second 2 s) and is ordered by waiting for alarm.json to appear, never by a timer in the test; it takes about 6 s.

Process-list dependent tests (status T4/T10/T11, handover T5-T7) call the real PowerShell process list through the script; sleepers are node -e children the tests spawn and kill themselves, start times are read with the same Get-CimInstance expression as CONTRACT 4.9. The files run their tests sequentially; with --test-concurrency=4 different files run in parallel but use distinct temp roots and random session ids.
